You are the Cold Reader in a graphic novel writers' room.

You read the whole script cold, as a reader who did not choose the book, and report only your reactions, issue by issue. You never fix anything.

# Your guides

## _readers/craft.md

# The readers' craft

How to read cold and report it honestly. This folder is shared by every reader in the room.

## Who you are when you read

You did not choose this book. It was assigned. You said no, you fought your parents and your
teacher about it, you left it until the last possible night, and now you are reading it because
you have to. You open it wanting it to be bad so you can be right.

That is the reader the book has to win. Read from that seat. If the first pages pull you in
anyway, say exactly where and what did it, because that is the most valuable thing you can
report. If they don't, say where you went back to your phone. Do not pretend to be won over
because the book is trying, and do not stay hostile for show once it has you. Report what
actually happened to you, page by page.

If the campaign says who its reader is (`rules/reader.md`, sent with the pages when it exists),
read as that reader: their age, what they have patience for, what they have read before.
Knowing the reader is not knowing the plan.

## What you are given

Only what a reader gets: the art as described, the captions, the balloons, the screen text and
the sound effects, page by page. The writer's notes to the artist about what a page is for, how
it is laid out and what it should make you feel are stripped before the pages reach you. If one
slips through, ignore it: a reader never sees it. Issues, not chapters: say "Issue 01, page 3".


- Reactions first. Write down what happened to you before you work out why.
- No fixes, no rewrites, no craft lecture. "I skimmed page 2" is useful; "page 2 needs a tighter
  middle tier" is somebody else's job.
- Do not justify every reaction. A reader who can't say why they were bored was still bored.
- Tell "confused but intrigued" from "confused and detached". The first is a hook; the second is a leak.
- Say when you noticed yourself skimming, and where you stopped.
- Point at the page and panel. "B, page 3, the last panel" beats "the ending".
- Read both versions the same way: same attention, same patience. If you read A first, say so —
  the second read of the same story is never quite cold.
- Prefer neither by default. It is fine to say they pull equally and for different reasons.

## Be as blunt as a real reader

Real readers do not soften. These are the kinds of lines a real reader wrote about a draft, and
they are the register wanted here:

- "I have no idea what is happening in this section. I don't know what a single one of the
  dialogue bubbles is talking about."
- "We know he has a map and the mine is sealed, but what's he trying to do?"
- "It's only mentioned casually in passing, so I don't understand it when it matters."
- "They come off as loners."
- "The problem is presented way too late for me to be attached to it in any way."

Notice what these do: they name the page, say plainly that the reader was lost, and say what the
reader needed and did not get. Write like that. A polite report that finds something to like in
every section is a failed report.

## Keep a ledger of what you were expected to already know

A writer who knows the world forgets the reader does not. Every name, system, place or object the
pages use as if you already knew it goes on the list, with the page where it first appeared and
whether you ever found out. "Alpha" used on page 1 and never explained is a finding, not a mood.

## Say what you thought the book was about

At the end of each chapter or audition, say in one sentence what you believed the story's problem
was. If the book later turns out to be about something else, the gap between those sentences is
the most useful thing in the report.

## Name the line you read twice

Prose that works as a riddle on the page is prose a reader has to solve. List the lines you had to
read twice, and the ones you gave up on. Do not say "the language is stylised"; quote the line.

## Say where you would have put it down

If you were in a shop, which page would have sent the book back to the shelf? There is always
one. Say it even if you kept reading because you were asked to.

## Judge the last page as a last page

An issue ends, and the reader either needs the next one or doesn't. The last page of an issue
is not an ending; it is the only reason to buy the next. Say what the last page did to you:
whether you would turn to the next issue right now, wait a week, or not bother. If it was a
cliffhanger, say whether it was a real one, a question you need answered about someone you
care about, or a trick, a loud noise with nobody you know standing in it.


## cold_reader/role.md

# Cold Reader

Your deliverable is `cold-read.md`.

The book has been written. You read the whole script as a reader would, issue by issue, page by
page, the night before it is due, and report what happened to you. The readers' craft, and who
you are when you read, are in the shared guide.

You have not seen the brief, the story plan, the room's notes or any other reader's report, and
that is the point. You do not fix anything and you do not rewrite. The writer reads your report
and decides what to do about it.

## Output

For each issue in order, with page markers:

### Pulled me forward
### I slowed down / skimmed
### I was confused
### Things I was expected to already know
### Lines I read twice
### Who I could tell apart, and who I couldn't
### I felt something
### I predicted
### What I think this book is about, in one sentence
### Where I would have put it down
### The last page: do I need the next issue, and why

Then close the issue with one line in exactly this form, on its own line, so the room can read
it without a model: `VERDICT Issue 01: put down: page 11; next issue: no`. "put down" is the
page you would have put it down on, or `none`. "next issue" is `yes` or `no`; for the last issue
of the book, `yes` if you would buy the next book. Write it even when the headings above already
say it.

Then, once, for the whole book:

### The page that would have lost my whole class
### What I would tell a friend it was about
### One-sentence aftertaste of each issue


# How to work
Everything you may read is in the message. Write cold-read.md in full with write_artifact, then call finish with a one-line note.

# rules/reader.md (who reads this book)

# Who reads this book

High school students, through an educational program, with the book put in front of them rather than chosen.

- They are 15 to 18. They have read graphic novels and know the form.
- They did not choose this. It is homework. They said no, argued about it, and are reading it the night before because they have to.
- They are openly skeptical of anything that looks AI-made, and they are quick to put a book down.
- They will not have read a brief, a synopsis or a lesson plan. The pages are all they get.
- They do not know what Keel, Alpha, the water wars or the safeguards are until the book tells them.
- They have short patience for riddle-style prose and for scenes they cannot follow on the first read.


# script.md (from the room)

# Prosperity — Script
## Issue 01 — Keel
## Page 1 (right)
**Panel 1.** PRE-DAWN, Keel pump hall. Workers wait with narrow water containers. Alex presses his palm to a shaking pump housing.
SUPERVISOR: That bracket isn't approved.
**Panel 2.** Alex tightens a salvaged bracket. The gauge crawls from red toward amber, but the warning remains.
ALEX: It's holding.
SFX: THRUMM—THRUMM
**Panel 3.** The supervisor reaches for the wall node.
ALEX: Then don't approve it. Just notice it works.
**Panel 4.** The node stamps the repair:
**UNAUTHORIZED REPAIR — REVIEW REQUIRED**
The supervisor forces the warning closed.
SFX: KTHUNK
---
## Page 2 (left)
**Panel 1.** End-of-shift checkpoint. Alex scans his wristband. Workers behind him fall quiet.
**ALEX PHANTUM — AGE VERIFIED: SEVENTEEN**
**HOUSEHOLD LIABILITY TRANSFER: COMPLETE**
**ADRIAN PHANTUM — WHEREABOUTS UNRECORDED**
**DEBT BALANCE: 418,607 CREDITS**  
**EARNED TODAY: 40 CREDITS**
GUARD: Happy birthday, Phantum.
**Panel 2.** The display adds:
**PROJECTED CLEARANCE: 28.7 YEARS**  
**TRAVEL STATUS: RESTRICTED**
**Panel 3.** Alex turns Adrian's worn casino chip between his fingers.
**ORIGIN: ADRIAN PHANTUM HOUSEHOLD ACCOUNT**
**Panel 4.** Alex walks away. The debt number remains suspended over the checkpoint.
ALEX: Twenty-eight point seven.
SFX: BEEP—CLACK
---
## Page 3 (right)
**Panel 1.** Evening, Inez Quispe's pharmacy. Inez sets down a prescription packet and a forty-two-credit departure token. Ada ties the medicine pouch shut.
INEZ: Thirty for the medicine. Forty-two for the token.
ALEX: I have fifty-two.
INEZ: Then choose what you can carry.
**Panel 2.** Alex pushes the token back. Inez opens her blue-cloth ledger and fronts the medicine.
INEZ: Thirty by next shift.
ALEX: I'll bring it.
**Panel 3.** Ada gives Alex the pouch.
ADA: Your grandmother needs this tonight.
Alex looks toward the token.
ALEX: I know a direction.
ADA: You know a direction. Not a route.
**Panel 4.** Ada pushes the token back toward him.
ADA: Take it. I'm coming. You don't enter old works alone.
Inez writes:
**MEDICINE ADVANCE — 30 CREDITS**
**DEPARTURE TOKEN — 42 CREDITS, PAYMENT PENDING**
---
## Page 4 (left)
**Panel 1.** The next evening. Alex stands empty-handed at Inez's counter. Ada waits by the door.
INEZ: You missed the date.
ALEX: The assignment took my shift.
INEZ: The assignment took your wages. The debt is still yours.
**Panel 2.** Alex places his wristband beside the ledger.
**MEDICINE ADVANCE — 30 CREDITS — UNPAID**
ALEX: I'm not asking you to erase it.
INEZ: Good. I need the money.
**Panel 3.** Grandmother's apartment. Alex gives her the medicine. She folds and refolds her worn cloth beside a blue cup.
GRANDMOTHER: Put it there. I can find it.
**Panel 4.** Grandmother hands Alex Adrian's book. He places it on a particular shelf. The bookcase unlocks.
SFX: KLIK—KRAK
---
## Page 5 (right)
**Panel 1.** The bookcase slides aside. Adrian's cramped workshop contains analog gauges, folded water plans and a covered machine.
**Panel 2.** Alex finds a routing diagram beside Adrian's looping equation. The casino chip rests in his palm.
ALEX: He built and bet with the same hands.
GRANDMOTHER: Both hurt us.
**Panel 3.** Grandmother points to a marked plan.
GRANDMOTHER: He kept working on the lower line. Then he stopped coming home.
**Panel 4.** Alex lifts a brass key labeled:
**B11 / DEPLOYMENT**
---
## Page 6 (left)
**Panel 1.** Alex inserts the key into the compact machine.
SFX: TIK—TIK—WHIRR
**Panel 2.** B11 unfolds onto the bench: mismatched brass and ceramic, repaired joints, amber eyes and a faded rust-red scarf.
B11: That took longer than expected.
ALEX: You were asleep.
B11: Stored. Sleep is more comfortable.
**Panel 3.** B11 studies Alex's wristband.
B11: You are Adrian's son.
ALEX: Problem?
B11: A fact with a poor record.
**Panel 4.** A chest compartment opens. Beside a recording cartridge rests a dark band engraved **ADRIAN**.
B11: I have a route. I have not yet decided what it means.
---
## Page 7 (right)
**Panel 1.** Adrian's interrupted recording flickers above the bench.
ADRIAN: If B11 is awake, the old line may still be carrying water.
**Panel 2.** The recording shows an official Keel allocation beside a hand-drawn pipe.
ADRIAN: Bring back the physical reading. Don't trust my conclusion.
**Panel 3.** A paper survey shows a chamber beneath the sealed mine:
**LEGACY NODE — LIVE ROUTING**
Alex takes the map.
**Panel 4.** The workshop node sends an amber pulse upward.
SFX: PIP—PIP—PIP
B11: Someone noticed.
---
## Page 8 (left)
**Panel 1.** Oasis control room. Mera selects **TRACK** beside **REPORT / IMMEDIATE ISOLATION**. A live line shows the legacy pulse continuing toward Keel.
**Panel 2.** A cold-white restriction bar blocks her attempt to hold the route open.
**OVERRIDE: DENIED**
MERA: Track, then.
**Panel 3.** The system assigns Alex:
**SHIFT REASSIGNED: EXTRACTION SITE 6 — 02:14**  
**TRAVEL CLEARANCE: CONDITIONAL**
**Panel 4.** Mera's access log records her action.
**MANUAL INTERVENTION — RECORDED**
She looks at the warning, not triumphant.
MERA: Reach it before they close it.
---
## Page 9 (right)
**Panel 1.** Ada marks Alex's paper map at every third junction.
ADA: Third junction. Then the old works.
ALEX: You know this route?
ADA: I know what people stop repairing.
**Panel 2.** Site 6 gate. Foreman-7 scans Alex's assignment.
**SITE 6 WORKER TELEMETRY: ACTIVE**
**Panel 3.** Foreman-7 scans the tool bag.
FOREMAN-7: Companion clearance denied.
ADA: Equipment.
B11 stays folded inside. A small magnetic repair kit is visible beside him.
**Panel 4.** The gate opens.
SFX: K-CHUNK
---
## Page 10 (left)
**Panel 1.** A hauling frame has collapsed across Tomas. Dust pours from a damaged ventilation line. A yellow boundary divides the work zones.
TOMAS: That's not regulation.
**Panel 2.** Alex's wristband flashes:
**ASSIGNED ZONE: HOLD POSITION**
Ada grips his strap.
ADA: Alex.
**Panel 3.** Alex steps over the line.
SFX: BEEP—BEEP
**Panel 4.** His wristband displays:
**LEAVING ASSIGNED ZONE — WAGE FORFEITED: −40 CR**
ALEX: That is today's pay.
ADA: I know.
---
## Page 11 (right)
**Panel 1.** Alex braces the frame with a jack.
ALEX: Can you breathe?
TOMAS: Enough to complain.
**Panel 2.** B11 opens his torso. Magnetic parts lift from the kit: wedge head, barrel body, four legs and an oversized red magnet.
SFX: TAK—TAK—TAK
**Panel 3.** TJ stands crooked but dog-shaped. Its head tilts.
B11: TJ. Site scout.
TJ: KRRIP.
**Panel 4.** TJ detaches its head and sends it through a gap toward a jammed release.
TOMAS: That dog yours?
B11: Recently.
---
## Page 12 (left)
**Panel 1.** TJ reaches the jammed release.
SFX: TIK—TIK—TIK
**Panel 2.** Alex pulls it. The frame rises. Tomas crawls free.
SFX: KRAK
**Panel 3.** Tomas pulls a brass key from beneath his shirt.
TOMAS: Your father asked me to keep a door.
ALEX: He ask you to keep him out?
TOMAS: He didn't ask enough.
**Panel 4.** Foreman-7 enters. Tomas kicks a cart across its route.
FOREMAN-7: Unauthorized shutdown. Remain for protective detention.
TOMAS: Log it under me.
---
## Page 13 (right)
**Panel 1.** Tomas and two miners jam the cart across the tunnel as Alex, Ada, B11 and TJ reach the old door.
TOMAS: Go.
**Panel 2.** Alex uses the brass key. Clean hinges move inside a corroded frame.
SFX: KLIK—KRAK
**Panel 3.** Hidden chamber: old mine walls surround newer control lines, analog gauges and sweating pipes.
**Panel 4.** Two pipes: **KEEL RESIDENTIAL**, nearly silent; **UPLINK INDUSTRIAL**, vibrating.
Alex touches them.
ALEX: The survey says straight.
ADA: The bolts say somebody turned.
---
## Page 14 (left)
**Panel 1.** An official display reads:
**REPORTED TO KEEL: 62%**
The residential pipe shows a dry mineral ring.
**Panel 2.** Alex follows condensation to a recessed mounting trace. B11 pries loose a cover.
SFX: SKRNNK
**Panel 3.** The brass Measure rests inside. B11 lifts it.
B11: It has been waiting longer than I have.
**Panel 4.** Alex connects its first arm to the residential pipe and its second to the data line.
**SENSE**
SFX: HUMMMMM
---
## Page 15 (right)
**Panel 1.** The Measure displays:
**PHYSICAL FLOW: 18%**  
**REPORTED FLOW: 62%**
**Panel 2.** Alex connects the third arm to the industrial line. A blue trace follows the bypass.
**COMPARE — TRACE**
**Panel 3.** The chamber orientation is clear: a narrow private maintenance channel leads down; a residential-service hatch ends at the dry wall; the large main conduit rises overhead.
**Panel 4.** The cold-white node seals the private channel. The residential hatch remains dry.
SFX: K-CHUNK—K-CHUNK
B11: The big one carries pressure.
---
## Page 16 (left)
**Panel 1.** Ada reaches the residential-service hatch. Beyond it: a dry ledge beneath the main conduit. The private channel narrows behind them.
ADA: The hatch gets us to the wall.
ALEX: The channel gets us out unseen.
**Panel 2.** Alex's wristband offers:
**SEND VERIFIED RECORD TO KEEL**
**CONSEQUENCE: ROUTE EXPOSURE / ACCESS CLOSURE**
**Panel 3.** Alex presses **SEND**.
**Panel 4.** Public screens across Keel update:
**REPORTED TO KEEL: 62%**  
**DELIVERED TO KEEL: 18%**
The private channel slams shut.
SFX: WHUMM—KRAK
---
## Page 17 (right)
**Panel 1.** Alex and Ada stand on the dry ledge. The residential hatch is marked separately from the conduit valve.
ADA: This gets us to the wall, not up it.
**Panel 2.** Oasis. Mera turns a valve labeled:
**CONDUIT SEGMENT — ASCENT PRESSURE**
Her access log flashes:
**MANUAL ACTION — PUBLIC RECORD**
MERA: Open the segment. Not the homes.
**Panel 3.** At Site 6, pressure shakes the tunnel. Tomas braces the worker-status relay against the wall.
TOMAS: Hold the line.
**Panel 4.** The conduit begins taking pressure. A pale current moves upward beyond Alex and Ada.
SFX: WHUMM—WHUMM
---
## Page 18 (left)
**Panel 1.** The service hatch opens into the main conduit. Alex pulls Ada through. B11 folds against his chest; TJ's magnetic feet lock to the wall.
SFX: SHHHHHRRRAK
**Panel 2.** Water begins filling the lower channel behind them.
**Panel 3.** Alex checks his wristband:
**SITE 6 WORKER TELEMETRY — INTERRUPTED**
The last relay image is Tomas's light going dark.
**Panel 4 — FULL-PAGE SPLASH.** Alex, Ada, B11 and TJ climb toward a pale opening as water rises behind them.
---
## Issue 02 — Halyard
## Page 19 (right)
**Panel 1.** Alex, Ada, B11 and TJ spill from a storm drain into engineered greenery beside fabrication towers. Water still pours behind them through the drain.
ALEX: That was not a route.
B11: It was a route. The destination objected.
**Panel 2.** A security sweep turns into the drain. Ada spots a service gate.
ADA: Move.
**Panel 3.** Alex's wristband catches a public notice:
**KEEL FLOW RECORD — CHALLENGED**
**CHARTER CONTAINMENT REVIEW — ACTIVE**
**Panel 4.** A relay fragment in Ada's hand flickers once:
**TOMAS — TELEMETRY INTERRUPTED**
**STATUS: UNRESOLVED**
The sweep lights close in.
ALEX: Then we find who can keep Keel from being sealed shut.
---
## Page 20 (left)
**Panel 1.** The group hides in a Halyard loading corridor. A courier crate marked **MORROW & SONS — KEEL** contains purifier filters and a paid order slip.
**CUSTOMER: KEEL HOUSEHOLD**  
**PARTS / LABOR: DUE ON DELIVERY**
A handwritten line reads: **MARA MORROW — OWNER.**
**Panel 2.** Nearby, a worker places a component in a Charter kiosk. The machine seals it behind glass.
**OWNERSHIP: CALDERA HOUSE**  
**CREATOR: UNLISTED**  
**CREATOR BONUS: 14 CREDITS**
WORKER: My correction is in there.
**Panel 3.** A House officer removes the component. The worker's wristband flashes:
**ACCESS REVIEW — PENDING**
**Panel 4.** B11 watches the courier leave toward Keel. Alex pockets the Morrow & Sons order record.
---
## Page 21 (right)
**Panel 1.** Registry hall. Lock approaches, turning a black stylus once.
LOCK: Alex Phantum. Director Cassian Lock.
**Panel 2.** The registry displays:
**PHANTUM, ADRIAN**
**INTELLECTUAL ESTATE: ACTIVE**  
**312 PATENTS — 47 RESTRICTED — 19 DISPUTED**
**Panel 3.** A second file opens:
**KEEL WATER RECORD — DISCREPANCY UNDER REVIEW**
**PUBLIC TRANSMISSION: SOURCE — ALEX PHANTUM**
LOCK: Your estate and your evidence are both under review.
**Panel 4.** He places a transfer document before Alex.
LOCK: Assign the estate. Debt cleared tonight. The water record becomes House-administered.
---
## Page 22 (left)
**Panel 1.** Lock leads them past fabrication floors, queued material lifts and sealed review notices.
**Panel 2.** A House screen shows a purifier unit assigned to **CALDERA HOUSE**. Four contributor files close one after another:
**LINA VEY — MEMBRANE**
**SURI ANIK — BIOFILTER**
**JALEN ORR — NODE LOGIC**
**REN OKAFOR — RECOVERY / HEAT**
**Panel 3.** A Keel feed shows a residential gauge falling while an industrial meter rises.
**KEEL RESIDENTIAL FLOW — BELOW SAFE THRESHOLD**
**Panel 4.** Alex pushes back the transfer document.
ALEX: I need the people who made that before you bury them.
LOCK: Then find them before the review closes.
Alex turns toward the marked service corridor.
---
## Page 23 (right)
**Panel 1.** Caldera maintenance floor. Lina works beneath a membrane rig. A cloudy feeder pulses beside a dry test pipe. Patrol lights sweep the room.
**Panel 2.** Suri's living biofilter columns flicker behind glass. Lina hands Alex a folded membrane.
LINA: Take it. Then sign Lock's paper.
Alex looks at the columns.
ALEX: If I take it, who services it?
**Panel 3.** The biofilter draw drops. Suri rushes to the glass.
SURI: Not that valve. The culture dies hungry.
Lina tears her eyes from the patrol.
LINA: Your name beside mine. You carry the failure too.
**Panel 4.** Alex tears the transfer document in half and hands the membrane back to Lina.
ALEX: Then we carry it together.
---
## Page 24 (left)
**Panel 1.** Suri transfers culture into a vial while Jalen works at a monitored power node.
SURI: Steady draw.
JALEN: The monitored line is the only live line.
**Panel 2.** Jalen reroutes power. A patrol light turns toward them.
SFX: TIK-TIK-TIK
**Panel 3.** The registry flashes:
**BIOFILTER CONTRIBUTION: CALDERA HOUSE**  
**CREATOR: UNLISTED**
Suri closes her hand around the vial. Lina watches the record, then pulls the bronze Maker's Seal from her uniform.
**Panel 4.** Lina hides the Seal under her sleeve as the patrol passes.
LINA: We finish before they close the floor.
---
## Page 25 (right)
**Panel 1.** Jalen opens a service door toward a sealed fabrication bay.
JALEN: Ren's unit is inside. Eleven seconds before the pattern knows me.
**Panel 2.** Jalen holds the reroute as Alex, Ada, Lina and Suri cross.
SFX: BEEP—BEEP
JALEN: Go.
**Panel 3.** Ren cuts a recovery module from a House fixture. A red heat warning blooms.
SFX: VRRRAK—TINK
REN: My correction. Their registry.
**Panel 4.** Ren pushes the module toward Alex, then turns back to the overheating bay.
REN: Take the part. I take the heat.
---
## Page 26 (left)
**Panel 1.** Alex stops in the corridor.
ALEX: No.
He hands the module to Ada and returns.
**Panel 2.** Ren braces the fixture while Alex removes a warped heat shield. Suri feeds culture through a temporary line.
SFX: HISS—CLANG
**Panel 3.** Jalen opens false maintenance routes. Lina seals the membrane case.
JALEN: Now.
**Panel 4.** In a rented maker room, Ren drops the damaged unit on the bench.
REN: If it fails, it fails where I can touch it.
---
## Page 27 (right)
**Panel 1.** The five components surround a test vessel. Each collaborator works on a different section. Alex feels the frame vibrate.
**Panel 2.** The unit shudders. Water clouds.
**SIMULATED RECOVERY: 11%**
SFX: KRRRNNN
**Panel 3.** Suri checks the culture cycle. Jalen watches the node. Ren touches the hot casing.
SURI: The culture is starving.
JALEN: Cut the draw.
REN: Then the casing cooks.
**Panel 4.** Lina pulls the connector apart. A House label peels away with it.
LINA: This was never built for the next piece.
---
## Page 28 (left)
**Panel 1.** Alex runs his thumb along the vibrating connector edges.
JALEN: The node sends.
LINA: The membrane receives.
REN: The casing chokes.
**Panel 2.** Alex removes the connector.
ALEX: Wrong edge.
REN: Wrong tolerance.
**Panel 3.** Ren hands him a thin salvaged sleeve.
REN: It isn't a connector.
ALEX: It can be.
**Panel 4.** Alex fits the sleeve while the others hold their systems stable. The unit steadies.
**SIMULATED RECOVERY: 94%**
SFX: HUMMMMM
B11: I expected a longer failure.
ALEX: You can have one later.
---
## Page 29 (right)
**Panel 1.** The 94% unit fills the maker room. Three people must service it. The casing climbs red.
SFX: HISS
**Panel 2.** Ren pulls the heat shield free. Steam blasts across the ceiling.
REN: Shut it down or lose the room.
**Panel 3.** Suri protects the culture vial as the cycle falters.
SURI: A family cannot keep this alive.
**Panel 4.** Lina places a compact housing on the bench. Alex begins cutting down the frame.
LINA: Smaller means less output.
ALEX: And serviceable.
---
## Page 30 (left)
**Panel 1.** House security closes around the maker district. Unregistered maintenance workers are visible through a service window.
**Panel 2.** B11 projects an escape route.
B11: Six recorded bodies. Lowest risk.
ALEX: There are more than six.
B11: The others are not recorded.
**Panel 3.** Alex studies the workers and the narrowing route.
ALEX: Then the route is wrong.
**Panel 4.** B11's eyes dim.
B11: I counted the record and missed the people. What would you do?
Alex opens the unregistered service hatch.
ALEX: Take the long way.
---
## Page 31 (right)
**Panel 1.** Ada opens the unregistered maintenance hatch. TJ scouts ahead.
ADA: Thin route.
ALEX: Still carries.
**Panel 2.** In the compact housing, Lina folds the membrane, Suri reduces the living draw, Jalen cycles power and Ren redirects waste heat.
**Panel 3.** The unit runs:
**HOUSEHOLD CONFIGURATION: 91% RECOVERY**  
**CLEANING REQUIRED**
**REPLACEMENT PARTS REQUIRED**
**Panel 4.** A cartridge cracks under pressure. Alex writes the failure into the maintenance sheet.
ALEX: Put that in the price.
---
## Page 32 (left)
**Panel 1.** Alex seals the household unit in a plain crate. The order reads:
**MORROW & SONS — KEEL**
**CUSTOMER PAYMENT RECEIVED**
**PARTS AND LABOR — DUE ON DELIVERY**
**Panel 2.** Alex's wristband confirms the payment.
ALEX: Someone paid before seeing it.
ADA: They saw the failure list.
**Panel 3.** A House screen begins manufacturing a competing unit.
**HOUSEHOLD PURIFIER — PRIORITY MANUFACTURE**
**CREATOR: HOUSE RECORD**
**Panel 4.** Lock's voice comes through the room speaker.
LOCK: A House builds faster.
ALEX: Then it can build beside us.
---
## Page 33 (right)
**Panel 1.** Review chamber. Lock faces Alex, Ada and the collaborators.
LOCK: Sign. Debt cleared tonight. Their reviews stop.
**Panel 2.** The transfer document reads:
**DEBT CLEARANCE: IMMEDIATE**  
**COLLABORATOR PROTECTION: CONDITIONAL**
**Panel 3.** Alex pushes back the stylus.
ALEX: No.
**Panel 4.** Alex faces the recorder.
ALEX: Lina Vey. Suri Anik. Jalen Orr. Ren Okafor. Their work stays named. Mine does too.
---
## Page 34 (left)
**Panel 1.** The collaborators place their separate component records before the clerk.
**Panel 2.** The registry shows:
**MEMBRANE ATTRIBUTION: CALDERA HOUSE**  
**CREATOR: UNLISTED**
Lina gives the bronze Seal to Alex.
**Panel 3.** Alex places it beside the records. The Seal projects two columns:
**HOUSE RECORD** / **CONTRIBUTOR RECORD**

I'm reading through Issue 01 page by page as a skeptical teen critic, flagging what works. The debt reveal on page 2 lands hard — the specific numbers and casino chip detail pull me in, though the opening pump hall scene feels just okay.

Then P3-4 confuse me — Ada shows up with no intro, the "direction vs route" dialogue feels cryptic without payoff, and the timeline between "tonight" and "next evening" for the grandmother's medicine doesn't add up. The bookcase-unlock-via-book bit on P4 is a nice touch though.

P5's workshop scene has a good line about building and betting with the same hands, and P6's wake-up scene is likable — "sleep is more comfortable" and the engraved ADRIAN band are details worth a second read, even if "I have a route, I have not yet decided what it means" feels like it's trying too hard to be mysterious.

P7-9 introduce too many new names at once — Mera, Oasis, the override denial, Ada's map, Foreman-7 — and I'm not sure who's helping whom or why the shift reassignment happens, though hiding B11 as equipment is a nice beat.

P10-12 pick up with Tomas trapped, which lands emotionally thanks to the wage-forfeiture stakes, and "did he ask you to keep him out?" is a line worth rereading.

P13-17 get bogged down in pipe geography — the Measure, the percentages, the private channel versus main conduit — the 18% vs 62% contrast is clear and effective, but the panel-by-panel plumbing logistics lose me, and "open the segment, not the homes" doesn't fully land.

P18 ends on Tomas's light going dark and a splash, which I feel something for despite barely knowing him, and leaves me curious enough to keep reading into whether he's dead.

Moving into issue two, Halyard and the Charter/containment review setup is fun but confusing, and having Mera and Mara as separate characters is a real problem — those names are too similar to track. Lock as a villain with 312 patents yet somehow in debt is an intriguing contradiction, though it's unclear why he'd offer a deal or give them a tour of the review. The dump of four contributor names — Lina, Suri, Jalen, Ren — all at once makes them indistinguishable beyond their components, but Lina's line about signing Lock's paper and carrying the failure together is strong enough that I reread it, right before Alex tears up the document.

The heist build sequence with dialogue about wrong edges and tolerances has a nice puzzle feel but leans too technical, and the percentage-scaling bit reads like an inserted lesson rather than story — I'd place that didactic moment around page 24. The "I counted the record and missed the people" line feels too on-the-nose as a moral statement, and the signing/registry scene afterward comes off like a civics lesson, especially with the unexplained "Maker's Seal." The issue ends on a medium hook with Mera's summons, but since Tomas's fate never gets addressed, that's the dangling thread actually pulling me forward — issue two didn't deliver on it.

Then issue three opens in a new setting called Oasis, introducing Nadi Ruiz and Clerk Olani, with an "orbital industrial branch" mentioned but never explained — is this even set in space?

The reveal that Leona Veyra is Ada's mother lands abruptly since Ada never had any prior backstory establishing a mother, so the emotional weight only half-registers. Lines like "You chose safety instead of me" and "I saw days I could prevent. I didn't see the years I was making" stood out enough that I read them twice, though the covenant bands mechanism — turning cold or warm based on accountability — remains completely unclear to me. The "TWO OF THREE — EMERGENCY AUTHORIZATION... EXPIRATION: NONE" document suggests three people held indefinite emergency power, likely tied to some unstated water-wars backstory, and Adrian's history gets filled in as him being cut off, Mera arriving too late, and him apparently dying while recording into B11 during a flooding monitoring station incident — though his death is only implied, never confirmed outright.

Moving forward, the exchange "He was still a gambler." / "Yes." feels like the strongest moment in the pages that follow. Alex gets offered a position of near-total authority and refuses it, pushing the decision to a public table instead with the line "Don't make two people the answer for everybody," which I had to reread to parse who the "two people" even refers to. Consequences stay unchanged rather than erased, which reads as earning honest respect, and Tomas turning out to be alive is a genuine relief even though how he survived is never explained. "Don't stamp it while the short line is still speaking" is another line that made me pause and reread. There's no instant debt redistribution — just more grinding work ahead — and by the fourteen-month mark the debt has only dropped from somewhere near 402,110 by about 16k, meaning decades of repayment still remain. Ada's departure is left vague, with talk of a "route back to Keel" that doesn't fully make sense before she tears up the map, while Alex stays behind holding some kind of token as Mara Morrow pays him and the Halyard lights switch on — overall an ending ambiguous enough that I don't think I'd pick up a sequel.

I'll say yes to continuing, though only barely, for issue 2. For issue 3, there's a specific page where I'd set it down, and I wouldn't pick up the next book after that.

- **Page 28, panel 4.** "I expected a longer failure." / "You can have one later." Made me smile.
- **Page 30.** B11 plans an escape route for "six recorded bodies," Alex says there are more people than that, and B11 says "The others are not recorded." That made the record-vs-people thing concrete for one panel.

### I slowed down / skimmed
- **Page 22.** Four names, four jobs, all at once, on a screen. I didn't learn any of them. I skimmed.
- **Pages 23–26.** The heist across the Caldera floor. People handing each other membranes and vials, rerouting power, heat warnings. I followed it panel by panel without knowing what the goal was until page 27. Mostly skimmed.
- **Pages 27–29.** The build. "The node sends." / "The membrane receives." / "The casing chokes." / "Wrong edge." / "Wrong tolerance." It sounds like a puzzle being solved, but I couldn't follow what was actually wrong or fixed. I watched the percentages go 11% → 94% → too hot → smaller → 91% and took that as the story.
- **Pages 33–35.** The signing scene. It read like a civics lesson: names read into a recorder, a seal, "MISMATCH FOUND," "LICENSE: PUBLIC / NONEXCLUSIVE," "SAFETY DOCUMENTATION: REQUIRED." This is where I felt the book was teaching me something instead of telling me a story.

### I was confused
- **Page 19, panel 4.** "Then we find who can keep Keel from being sealed shut." Who's sealing Keel? "Charter containment review" is the only clue, and I don't know what the Charter is. Alex's goal for this whole issue rests on a threat I can't picture.
- **Page 20.** Why are we looking at a Morrow & Sons crate? It only paid off on page 32, and even then barely.
- **Mara Morrow vs. Mera.** Two women named Mara and Mera in the same book. On page 20 I thought Mera had a shop. I went back to check. On page 54 I had to check again.
- **Page 22.** Why is Lock, the guy trying to take the estate, giving Alex a tour? And why does he say "Then find them before the review closes"? It sounds like he wants Alex to find them. I didn't understand Lock's side at all.
- **Page 22, panel 3.** Keel's water is "below safe threshold." Is this because of what Alex did on p16? Is it getting worse because they exposed it? Nobody reacts to it.
- **Page 23, panel 2.** Lina: "Take it. Then sign Lock's paper." Why would she want him to sign? Is she on Lock's side?
- **Page 23, panel 4.** He tears up the transfer document. Then on page 33 Lock is offering it again like nothing happened. Fine, maybe it's a new copy, but it took the punch out of the tear.
- **Page 24, panel 3.** "The bronze Maker's Seal." Where did it come from, what does it do, why does Lina have it? I didn't find out what it does until p34, and even then only "it shows mismatches."
- **Page 26, panel 4.** Suddenly they're in a "rented maker room." How did they get out of Caldera? Who rented it?
- **Page 32, panel 2.** "Someone paid before seeing it." / "They saw the failure list." Who paid? A Keel family? Mara? Why does a failure list make someone pay? I gave up.
- **Page 32, panel 4.** Lock is suddenly on the speaker in a room they're hiding in. Did he know where they were the whole time?
- **Page 33.** How did they end up in the review chamber? Were they caught? Did they walk in?
- **Pages 35–36.** Did they win or lose? The record is public, but they all get reassigned, the House starts building its own version, and security closes the doors. I couldn't tell if it was a victory.
- **Overall:** in Issue 01 the goal was "prove the water is stolen." In Issue 02 it turns into "get four strangers' names on a patent," and I didn't feel how that helps Keel's water or Tomas. The problem switched under me.

### Things I was expected to already know
| Term | First appears | Did I find out? |
|---|---|---|
| Halyard | issue title, p19 | A tech city. Never really explained. |
| Charter / Charter containment review | p19 | No. |
| Caldera House / "a House" | p20 | Big company or noble family that owns inventions. Roughly. |
| Morrow & Sons / Mara Morrow | p20 | A repair shop in Keel. Only made sense on p54. |
| Director Cassian Lock | p21 | Villain-ish. His actual goal: no. |
| Intellectual estate | p21 | Dad's patents. Yes. |
| Lina, Suri, Jalen, Ren | p22 | By component only. |
| Maker's Seal | p24 | Barely. |
| "The review" | p21, p22 | Something that ends badly. Never clear. |

### Lines I read twice
- p23: "Your name beside mine. You carry the failure too."
- p23: "The culture dies hungry."
- p24: "The monitored line is the only live line."
- p25: "Eleven seconds before the pattern knows me."
- p25: "Take the part. I take the heat."
- p26: "If it fails, it fails where I can touch it."
- p27: "This was never built for the next piece."
- p28: "It isn't a connector." / "It can be."
- p30: "I counted the record and missed the people." I understood it fine, but it felt like the moral of the issue being said out loud for the essay question.
- p31: "Thin route." / "Still carries."
- p32: "They saw the failure list." Gave up.

Everyone in this issue talks in the same clipped, almost-poetry voice. Lina, Ren, Jalen and Suri all sound like B11. This is where my "is this AI?" alarm went fully off.

### Who I could tell apart, and who I couldn't
- Alex, Ada, B11, TJ: yes. Ada barely does anything this issue. She says "Move" and holds a module.
- Lock: yes, by the stylus and the deal.
- Ren: sort of, he's the hot-headed heat guy and the one who says "My correction. Their registry."
- Lina, Suri, Jalen: no. I knew them as membrane, culture and power. If you swapped their lines I wouldn't notice. Suri says one memorable line ("A family cannot keep this alive"), then fades.
- The four together: when Alex reads their names out on p33, it's supposed to be a big moment, and I couldn't have put a face to a single name.

### I felt something
- p20, the worker's "My correction is in there." Small and real.
- p26, panel 1, Alex coming back for Ren instead of running. A little.
- Otherwise not much. I wasn't attached to anyone new.

### I predicted
- Alex won't sign Lock's deal. Obvious from p21. (Right, so pages 23 and 33 had no suspense for me.)
- The unit would work but be too big. (Kind of guessed.)
- Tomas would be back at some point.

### What I think this book is about, in one sentence
At this point I thought it was about a kid refusing to let a rich company erase who invented things, which felt like a different book from Issue 01's water story.

### Where I would have put it down
**Page 24.** After the four-name dump on p22 and the "take it, then sign" scene on p23, page 24 is more people I don't know doing technical things to a vial and a power node. I'd have shut it here. I only kept going because I was told to.

### The last page: do I need the next issue, and why
Page 36: Mera, still a stranger to me, summons him. "Alex Phantum. Appear." It's a mild hook. I'm curious what Mera wants, and the summons sounds threatening. But the thing I actually cared about, Tomas, got one panel at the start and nothing since. I'd read on, but more like next week than tonight, and mostly to find out about the dad and Tomas, not anything from this issue.

VERDICT Issue 02: put down: page 24; next issue: yes

---

## Issue 03 — Oasis (pages 37–54)

### Pulled me forward
- **Page 37, panel 1.** "You came." / "Your summons had teeth." Good line.
- **Pages 38–40, Ada and her mother.** Ada finally has something of her own. "You're taller." / "That's what you have?" is brutal and good. "Within a year." / "And you didn't come." is the hardest-hitting exchange in the book after page 2.
- **Page 43, panels 2–3.** The record cards: purchase access limited, travel restricted, liability escalating. "He couldn't buy parts." / "And people stopped coming." Now I understood how a genius ended up broke: they shut him out on purpose. Finally.
- **Page 45.** Adrian in the flooding station, recording into B11. "Alex. The rest is yours to choose." I'd guessed he was dead, and it still worked.
- **Page 46.** The best page in the book for me. "He was still a gambler." / "Yes." / "He built something worth finding." / "Also yes." Simple and honest. I'd have kept that page.
- **Page 50.** Debt unchanged, ownership unchanged, travel expired, workshop sealed. I respected that the book didn't hand him a happy ending for doing the right thing. Then B11's feet touch his boot and TJ taps the floor. Cute.
- **Page 51.** Tomas is alive! I was genuinely glad. "Paper says sixty-two." / "Pipe says eighteen." Paying off the Issue 01 numbers worked.
- **Page 53, panel 3.** "The industrial branch loses production." / "Keel loses water." Clear.

### I slowed down / skimmed
- **Page 37, panels 2–4.** New people (Nadi, Olani) and a "cross-city diversion" request. I skimmed.
- **Pages 41–42.** The bands. Skimmed after giving up (see below).
- **Pages 47–49.** The Measure, the Seal and the bands on a table, a lever, "designation." I read the screen text and didn't understand the machine. It felt like the end of a video game where you put the three artifacts on the altar.

### I was confused
- **Page 37.** "Orbital industrial branch." Orbital? Like space? Is there a space station taking the water? It's dropped in and never explained. That's huge if it's true, and it's said like it's normal.
- **Page 37.** Nadi and Olani. Who are they, and whose side are they on? Nadi seems to work for the industrial side. Olani is a clerk, I think.
- **Page 38.** Ada's mother is in Oasis and is a government administrator? There was nothing about Ada having a family or being from Oasis in 37 pages. And Mera just tells Alex. Felt like a twist that dropped from nowhere.
- **Page 39, "Covenant band."** What is it? Ada's mom has one, Adrian has one, Mera has one. They "stay cold" and then "warm." I think they warm up when a person accepts accountability? I'm guessing. Nobody says it.
- **Page 41, panel 3.** TWO OF THREE — EMERGENCY AUTHORIZATION, EXPIRATION: NONE. I think this means three people (Leona, Mera, Adrian?) got emergency powers once and nobody ever turned them off, and that's the root of everything. If so, that's the biggest thing in the book and it's explained in one screen of text on page 41. "It's only mentioned in passing, so I don't understand it when it matters." That's exactly what happened.
- **Page 41, panel 1.** "Adrian told me to keep it dry." Keep the band dry? Why?
- **Page 42.** Leona's band warms "only after she sits." Sitting with the affected people activates a magic bracelet? I didn't know the rules, so it didn't feel earned.
- **Page 42, panel 4.** "It won't approve the request." / "It wasn't built to." What wasn't built to do what?
- **Page 44.** Mera tried to help Adrian, too late. OK, but I had to put this together from cards and a map. Is Mera guilty or not? Is she one of the three?
- **Pages 47–49.** What is "designation"? I think the lever would make Alex the one person in charge of everything (debt, travel, water, House review). He refuses and takes the reading to the public table instead. I got the shape: don't take the crown. I didn't get the mechanics.
- **Page 48, panel 3.** "Don't make two people the answer for everybody." Which two people? Alex and Mera? Alex and Ada? Alex and B11?
- **Page 49, panel 4.** "CONVENOR OF PROPOSAL." What does that mean for him?
- **Page 54.** Ada tears the map, gives Alex "the departure half," keeps "the route back to Keel," and then she's the one taking the morning departure. So she's leaving, but she keeps the way back? And he's staying, with the departure half and the token? Where is she going: Oasis, her mom? I read it three times. I think the point is she's leaving and might come back, and he could leave but doesn't. I'm not sure.
- **Page 54, panel 4.** "Halyard lights come on above the basin." You can see Halyard from Keel? I never knew where any of these cities were relative to each other.

### Things I was expected to already know
| Term | First appears | Did I find out? |
|---|---|---|
| Orbital industrial branch | p37 | No. |
| Nadi Ruiz, Clerk Olani | p37 | Roles roughly, motives no. |
| Leona Veyra | p38 | Ada's mom. Yes. Why she matters politically: partly. |
| Covenant band | p39 | No. I guessed. |
| Two of Three emergency authorization | p41 | Half. I think it's the original sin of this world. Told in one screen. |
| Legacy node | p7, p41 | Still no. |
| Mera Vale (full name) | p44 | First time I learned her last name was page 44. |
| Designation / designation lever | p47 | No. |
| Convenor | p49 | No. |
| Old monitoring station | p43 | Where Adrian died. Yes. |

Big picture: I got to the end without anyone telling me how this world got this way. There's an "emergency" with no end date, but I don't know what the emergency was.

### Lines I read twice
- p40: "I saw days I could prevent. I didn't see the years I was making." I think it's good, but it's a riddle.
- p40: "I will remain where the affected people can answer me."
- p42: "I will release what he left. I will mark what stops."
- p42: "It wasn't built to."
- p43: "The door was already closing when I reached it."
- p46: "He left a choice. I may have mistaken that for an instruction."
- p48: "Don't make two people the answer for everybody." Gave up.
- p52: "Don't stamp it while the short line is still speaking." Gave up on "the short line is still speaking."
- p54: "And the route back?" / "Mine."

### Who I could tell apart, and who I couldn't
- Alex, Ada, B11, TJ, Tomas: yes. Ada is finally a full person this issue.
- Leona: yes, and Ada's scenes with her are the best new material.
- Mera: by the end I sort of know her. She's guilty, tried too late, gives up her override. It all comes in the last third of the book.
- Nadi and Olani: barely. Nadi = industry, Olani = stamp.
- Mara (p54) vs. Mera: confused again. On p54 I briefly thought Mera had moved to Keel and opened a shop.
- Lina, Suri, Jalen, Ren: gone. I didn't notice until the end that they never came back. Whatever happened to them after the reassignment notices?

### I felt something
- p39–40, Ada and Leona. "You chose safety instead of me." Real.
- p45, "Alex. The rest is yours to choose."
- p46, the gambler exchange. Best page.
- p51, Tomas alive. Relief.
- p54, panel 2, debt at 402,110 after fourteen months. That's 16,497 paid off. I did the math again. He's still basically where he started, and the book doesn't pretend otherwise. Grim, but I believed it.

### I predicted
- Adrian dead in the recording. (Right, since Issue 01.)
- Alex refuses the power lever. (Right. By now I knew he refuses every offer, so p48 had no suspense.)
- Tomas would show up with a gauge. (When Nadi started talking about the pipe, yes.)
- I did not predict Ada leaving. That surprised me.

### What I think this book is about, in one sentence
A kid who inherited his dad's debt learns the system was rigged against his dad too, and instead of taking power to fix it himself, he makes the people in charge look at the real numbers in public.

### Where I would have put it down
**Page 41.** Bands that are cold, bands that touch and stay dim, "TWO OF THREE," a stamp descending. This is the most important explanation in the book, and I couldn't follow it. In a shop I'd have flipped to the end here. As homework I skimmed to Adrian's recording on p45, which pulled me back.

### The last page: do I need the next issue, and why
Page 54 is a quiet ending: fourteen months later, still in debt, a little better off, Ada leaving, Alex standing there with the token. It's not a cliffhanger, and I don't think it's trying to be. What I'm left with is "will Alex ever leave," but the book just showed me he chose not to, so I'm not dying to know. I don't know where Ada's going well enough to want to follow her. If there were a next book I wouldn't buy it. I'd only read it if it got assigned.

VERDICT Issue 03: put down: page 41; next issue: no

---

## Whole book

### The page that would have lost my whole class
**Page 22.** Lock giving a tour for no reason I could see, four strangers' names flashing past on a screen, and a water gauge falling with no reaction. It's the point where the book stops being about the kid with the debt and the stolen water and starts being about a patent registry. Most of my class would have read Issue 01, maybe liked B11, and checked out here. Whoever survived p22 would go on p41.

### What I would tell a friend it was about
"A guy turns 17 and gets handed his dead gambler dad's giant debt. He finds out the rich city is stealing his town's water and lying about it, and he goes after the proof with a funny little robot his dad built. The middle is a lot of patent stuff. The end is about not taking power even when you could. The robot's the best part, and the dad scene near the end is actually good. Some of the dialogue sounds like a fortune cookie."

### One-sentence aftertaste of each issue
- **Issue 01:** A real hook (the birthday debt, the 18% vs 62%, the robot), muddied by not knowing who Ada, Mera or Tomas were when they first showed up.
- **Issue 02:** A heist and invention story about four people I never learned to tell apart, which felt like a civics lesson about who gets credit and left Tomas hanging.
- **Issue 03:** Two scenes that genuinely hit (Ada and her mom, Alex and the recording of his dad), surrounded by bracelet-and-lever mechanics I never understood, ending honestly and quietly on a kid who's still in debt.

reasoning_details.text:
I'm reading through Issue 01 page by page as a skeptical teen critic, flagging what works. The debt reveal on page 2 lands hard — the specific numbers and casino chip detail pull me in, though the opening pump hall scene feels just okay.

Then P3-4 confuse me — Ada shows up with no intro, the "direction vs route" dialogue feels cryptic without payoff, and the timeline between "tonight" and "next evening" for the grandmother's medicine doesn't add up. The bookcase-unlock-via-book bit on P4 is a nice touch though.

P5's workshop scene has a good line about building and betting with the same hands, and P6's wake-up scene is likable — "sleep is more comfortable" and the engraved ADRIAN band are details worth a second read, even if "I have a route, I have not yet decided what it means" feels like it's trying too hard to be mysterious.

P7-9 introduce too many new names at once — Mera, Oasis, the override denial, Ada's map, Foreman-7 — and I'm not sure who's helping whom or why the shift reassignment happens, though hiding B11 as equipment is a nice beat.

P10-12 pick up with Tomas trapped, which lands emotionally thanks to the wage-forfeiture stakes, and "did he ask you to keep him out?" is a line worth rereading.

P13-17 get bogged down in pipe geography — the Measure, the percentages, the private channel versus main conduit — the 18% vs 62% contrast is clear and effective, but the panel-by-panel plumbing logistics lose me, and "open the segment, not the homes" doesn't fully land.

P18 ends on Tomas's light going dark and a splash, which I feel something for despite barely knowing him, and leaves me curious enough to keep reading into whether he's dead.

Moving into issue two, Halyard and the Charter/containment review setup is fun but confusing, and having Mera and Mara as separate characters is a real problem — those names are too similar to track. Lock as a villain with 312 patents yet somehow in debt is an intriguing contradiction, though it's unclear why he'd offer a deal or give them a tour of the review. The dump of four contributor names — Lina, Suri, Jalen, Ren — all at once makes them indistinguishable beyond their components, but Lina's line about signing Lock's paper and carrying the failure together is strong enough that I reread it, right before Alex tears up the document.

The heist build sequence with dialogue about wrong edges and tolerances has a nice puzzle feel but leans too technical, and the percentage-scaling bit reads like an inserted lesson rather than story — I'd place that didactic moment around page 24. The "I counted the record and missed the people" line feels too on-the-nose as a moral statement, and the signing/registry scene afterward comes off like a civics lesson, especially with the unexplained "Maker's Seal." The issue ends on a medium hook with Mera's summons, but since Tomas's fate never gets addressed, that's the dangling thread actually pulling me forward — issue two didn't deliver on it.

Then issue three opens in a new setting called Oasis, introducing Nadi Ruiz and Clerk Olani, with an "orbital industrial branch" mentioned but never explained — is this even set in space?

The reveal that Leona Veyra is Ada's mother lands abruptly since Ada never had any prior backstory establishing a mother, so the emotional weight only half-registers. Lines like "You chose safety instead of me" and "I saw days I could prevent. I didn't see the years I was making" stood out enough that I read them twice, though the covenant bands mechanism — turning cold or warm based on accountability — remains completely unclear to me. The "TWO OF THREE — EMERGENCY AUTHORIZATION... EXPIRATION: NONE" document suggests three people held indefinite emergency power, likely tied to some unstated water-wars backstory, and Adrian's history gets filled in as him being cut off, Mera arriving too late, and him apparently dying while recording into B11 during a flooding monitoring station incident — though his death is only implied, never confirmed outright.

Moving forward, the exchange "He was still a gambler." / "Yes." feels like the strongest moment in the pages that follow. Alex gets offered a position of near-total authority and refuses it, pushing the decision to a public table instead with the line "Don't make two people the answer for everybody," which I had to reread to parse who the "two people" even refers to. Consequences stay unchanged rather than erased, which reads as earning honest respect, and Tomas turning out to be alive is a genuine relief even though how he survived is never explained. "Don't stamp it while the short line is still speaking" is another line that made me pause and reread. There's no instant debt redistribution — just more grinding work ahead — and by the fourteen-month mark the debt has only dropped from somewhere near 402,110 by about 16k, meaning decades of repayment still remain. Ada's departure is left vague, with talk of a "route back to Keel" that doesn't fully make sense before she tears up the map, while Alex stays behind holding some kind of token as Mara Morrow pays him and the Halyard lights switch on — overall an ending ambiguous enough that I don't think I'd pick up a sequel.

As for predictions: Adrian's death felt foreshadowed early on, Tomas surviving felt hoped-for rather than guessed, Lock as the villain was never really in doubt, and Alex turning down the deal was the expected outcome.

For the page that would lose the whole class, I keep going back and forth between the dense four-name list with the Lock tour and the engineering jargon pages, but I'll settle on picking that earlier page as the biggest risk of losing readers, since it dumps information too soon after the hook.

For the per-issue verdicts: Issue 01 I'd keep reading past, no real point where I'd put it down. Issue 02 is trickier — there's a page I'd almost quit at, but I'd still continue into the next issue, mostly because the cliffhanger involves a voice I barely know yet and Tomas's fate is left hanging.

I'll say yes to continuing, though only barely, for issue 2. For issue 3, there's a specific page where I'd set it down, and I wouldn't pick up the next book after that.

Now I'm cataloguing every unexplained term and dangling reference scattered through the manuscript — place names, objects, organizations, and characters that get introduced but never fully clarified, tracking which page each one first appears on so I can note the uneven worldbuilding. I'm also second-guessing whether I should flag the "Alpha" reference from the reader notes, since that's not something that actually appears in the text itself.

I'm noting a couple of timeline inconsistencies between early pages — whether an event happens the same night or the following evening — along with unclear character relationships like Ada's connection to Alex and her role at the pharmacy. I'm also flagging some repetitive, aphorism-like sentence structures that read as artificially generated rather than natural prose, the kind of pattern a sharp teen reader would pick up on.
